title: Vyshka manifest bodies
description: Machine-readable companion to spec/protocol.md section 6. The prose document is normative: where the two disagree, the prose wins. Like envelopes.schema.json this is a library of definitions with no root constraint: reference `#/$defs/manifestPublish` for the manifest.publish body and `#/$defs/manifestReject` for the hub's answer to a refused one. The `paramsSchema` definition describes the *shape* of the section 6.1 schema subset; the closed-keyword rule (anything outside the subset rejects the manifest) is enforced by hubs, not expressible here.

label.description: Human-facing display name. Advisory; the hub never routes on it.

namespace.description: The owning mod's namespace, for display grouping and token scoping (section 10).

paramsSchema.title: Section 6.1 schema subset
paramsSchema.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) restricted to: a single `type`, `enum`, `not` in the one form `{"enum": [...]}`, `required`, `properties`, `items`, numeric bounds, annotation-only `default`, the `context` and `kvNamespace` annotations on string schemas, and the vendor UI hint `x-vyshka-widget`. A hub MUST reject a manifest whose schema carries any other keyword, because it validates dispatch payloads against these schemas and cannot enforce what it does not implement. Integer constants (bounds, enum members) MUST lie strictly within ±2^53; a hub rejects what a float64 round-trip would change (section 6.1).

enum.description: Allowed values, compared by deep equality.

not.description: Values the field must not take, compared by deep equality as enum compares (exactly, so a string's case matters). Enforced like any other keyword: a dispatch naming one fails validation. This is the only form of not the subset admits; any other rejects the manifest (section 6.4). A UI offering values for the field shows a listed one as unavailable and refuses it before dispatch (section 6.1). null reads as no exclusion.

required.description: Property names an object instance must carry.

default.description: Annotation only: surfaced to UIs, never enforced.

context.description: Annotation on a `type: string` schema: the custom context (or contexts, none repeated) the manifest declares whose enumerated entries a UI offers as the field's values, the referenceKey as the value and the label as the text (section 6.1). Never enforced against a dispatched value. A manifest naming an undeclared context here, or putting it on a non-string schema, is rejected (section 6.4); null reads as no annotation.

kvNamespace.description: Annotation on a `type: string` schema: the key/value namespace, one the manifest declares in kvNamespaces, whose keys a UI offers as the field's values through the list-keys read (section 6.1). Never enforced against a dispatched value. A manifest naming an undeclared namespace here, or putting it on a non-string schema, is rejected (section 6.4); null reads as no annotation.

x-vyshka-widget.description: UI hint (itemlist, vector, player, webhook, ...). Deliberately open-ended: it never constrains the data model, so an unknown hint must not reject a manifest.

code.description: Unique within a server. SHOULD be {namespace}.{name}.

context.description: A built-in context (world, player, vehicle, object) or one the manifest declares.

id.description: Unique within the manifest. The built-in contexts (world, player, vehicle, object) cannot be declared as a manifest's own (section 6.2); a hub rejects the manifest (section 6.4).

manifestPublish.title: manifest.publish body
manifestPublish.description: Body of the manifest.publish envelope (section 6). Sent at session start and at any later moment; a runtime republish costs one message, not a server restart. A JSON null where an optional field could appear reads as the field being absent (section 6.4); length limits count Unicode code points.

game.description: Lowercase game identifier. Advisory here; enrollment enforces the match.

manifestRevision.description: Plugin-owned and monotonic, within [1, 2^53). A higher revision replaces the stored manifest; an equal or lower one is ignored. Advances only on acceptance, so a corrected manifest may be republished at a revision that was rejected.

kvNamespaces.description: The key/value namespaces (section 12) this plugin may operate on; the sole source of a plugin's KV access. Duplicates reject the manifest, as does an entry outside the namespace grammar: this field grants access, so a malformed grant fails at publish time (section 6.6).

manifestReject.title: manifest.reject body
manifestReject.description: Body of the manifest.reject envelope (section 6.4): the hub's answer to a manifest.publish it refused. The refusal never fails the poll or the session; this envelope is how the plugin learns.

envelopeId.description: The `id` of the refused manifest.publish envelope.

manifestRevision.description: The refused revision, present when it was readable from the rejected body.

path.description: Dotted path into the rejected body; "" for its root.

errors.description: What was wrong, capped by the hub (reference cap: 20).

contextEnumerate.title: context.enumerate body
contextEnumerate.description: Body of the context.enumerate envelope (section 6.2, hub -> plugin): a request for the members of one declared custom context. Optional on the hub side; a plugin answers every one it receives with a context.entries reply.

requestId.description: Hub-assigned and opaque; the reply echoes it.

context.description: The declared context id being enumerated.

contextEntries.title: context.entries body
contextEntries.description: Body of the context.entries envelope (section 6.2, plugin -> hub): the members of one custom context, answering a context.enumerate. A request for a context the plugin does not declare is answered with an empty list and a reason.

referenceKey.description: What the hub hands back verbatim as an action's referenceKey.

position.description: As in section 8.3: two or three finite numbers in the game's own map frame, advisory, for display. Absent and null both read as no position.

data.description: Mod-specific extras. Absent and null both read as an empty object.

reason.description: Why entries is empty when the request named a context this plugin does not declare.
